item.title: Trump says he's ending restrictions on climate-warming methane from oil drilling
item.description: President Donald Trump said that his administration is "terminating" a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: When an invasive fish is also tasty, Maryland schoolkids can help 'eat the problem'
item.description: The Chesapeake Bay, home to blue crabs and striped bass, has a new apex predator: the blue catfish. It's invasive and voracious. It's also delicious, which officials hope might help save the bay.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Arizona adds U.S.'s newest national park, but National Park Service remains underfunded
item.description: President Trump, famous for stripping protections from national monuments, is signing a bill to turn one into a national park. The land in southern Arizona is biologically rich and scenic.

item.title: United Nations report highlights significant increase in U.S. climate pollution
item.description: The U.S. is the only major economy where planet-warming pollution dramatically increased last year. The United Nations warns the planet is on track for catastrophic warming.

item.title: Oyster aid efforts in the Chesapeake
item.description: Two people — an eco-evangelist and an engineer — are taking different approaches to support the same critical ingredient in the Chesapeake Bay: oysters.

item.description: We journey with a hiker as he records the sounds of 2,600 miles of wilderness on the Pacific Crest Trail.

item.title: This summer's fire season was bigger and deadlier than most
item.description: Historic drought had western states entering summer anxious about wildfires. Some suffered significant destruction and death, but there were wins, too.

item.title: A Kelvin wave raised sea levels on the West Coast. More are coming
item.description: A large underwater wave moved up the West Coast, raising sea levels. Scientists say it's driven by El Niño and it's going to happen again.

item.title: Those lake "weeds" actually keep lakes healthy
item.description: Some people may think that plants that grow in lakes are weeds that should be removed, but ecologists say native aquatic plants keep lakes healthy. They also prevent invasive species from taking over.

item.title: Group that plants fruit trees in vacant lots grows to cities nationwide
item.description: A Kansas City group set up to help volunteers plant fruit trees in vacant city lots has quickly branched out across the country with almost 850 orchards in 17 cities with more to come.
